stances.claim: The three constitutional 'angels' -- Sereno, Morales, and Tan -- are independent of the President and owe their loyalty first to the Constitution; they will outlast P-Noy's term.
Independence of constitutional officers from the President, Congress, business, labor, NGOs, and media is the most important of the four INs.
The shift from DoJ prosecution (1935 Constitution) to OMB investigation (1987) reflects the lesson that partisan prosecution of officials under the old system corrupted accountability.
The three other female appointees -- de Lima, Soliman, Henares, Herbosa, and Abad -- are under the President's direction and their actions are appealable to the Office of the President.

notable_anecdotes: Aquino's 'uncanny knack and good luck' in appointing a 'gutsy corps of angels' -- the author's characterization of the President's record of female appointment choices as a distinctive personnel style.
Herbosa described as a 'brilliant lawyer-descendant of Jose Rizal' -- the most striking personal biography detail in the list of Aquino's women appointees.
PMS Chief Julia Abad described as able to 'read P-Noy's mind like no one else' -- the most intimate institutional-proximity description in the column.
Both Morales and Tan will outlast P-Noy's six-year term -- highlighting that the constitutional officers are designed to be a check even on the president who appointed them.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban profiles President Aquino's 'gutsy corps of angels' -- female appointees to critical posts -- distinguishing three constitutional officers independent of the President from three others under his direct supervision. The three independent constitutional angels: (1) CJ Maria Lourdes P. A. Sereno, first woman CJ, whose loyalty is first to the Constitution (CIPI: competence, integrity, probity, independence -- with independence most paramount), chosen from the JBC list without owing any debt to P-Noy; (2) Ombudsman Conchita Carpio Morales, the 'protector of the people,' authorized under RA 6770 to investigate any public official for illegal, unjust, improper, or inefficient acts -- not impeachable officials directly but for the purpose of impeachment complaint filing, ill-gotten wealth civil cases, and post-term criminal indictments; (3) COA Chair Grace Pulido Tan, sentinel of government assets, with a 7-year fixed term and fiscal independence -- both Morales and Tan will outlast P-Noy's term. The three dependent officials: DOJ Secretary de Lima (prosecution arm, determines probable cause for crime), DSWD Secretary Soliman (CCT program), and BIR Commissioner Henares (RATE program, tax cases against celebrities and businessmen), plus SEC Chair Herbosa (investor protection; 'brilliant lawyer-descendant of Jose Rizal') and PMS Chief Julia Abad (presidential gatekeeper who 'can read P-Noy's mind like no one else'). The author notes that the shift from 1935's partisan DoJ prosecution to 1987's independent OMB reflects the lesson that partisan accountability mechanisms are unreliable.
